```{r model_fit, eval=FALSE}
  tune::fit_resamples(.,
                      resamples = cv_splits_geo,
                      control   = control,
                      metrics   = metrics)

glmnet_tuned <- glmnet_wf %>%
  tune::tune_grid(.,
                  resamples = cv_splits_geo,
                  grid      = glmnet_grid,
                  control   = control,
                  metrics   = metrics)

rf_tuned <- rf_wf %>%
  tune::tune_grid(.,
                  resamples = cv_splits_geo,
                  grid      = rf_grid,
                  control   = control,
                  metrics   = metrics)

xgb_tuned <- xgb_wf %>%
  tune::tune_grid(.,
                  resamples = cv_splits_geo,
                  grid      = xgb_grid,
                  control   = control,
                  metrics   = metrics)
```

```{r message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
           control   = control,

## Fit and Extract final model
```

### Model Validation and Comparison

After applying the models to the test set, we evaluate and compare models' accuracy using Mean Absolute Error (MAE), Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE) and prediction v.s. actual value scatter plot.

+ **Mean Absolute Error (MAE)**: This tells us how much, on average, our model's predicted price is off from the real price. For example, if the model says a house is worth $310,000, but it actually sold for $300,000, the error is $10,000. MAE takes the average of all these errors. So if MAE is $15,000, that means our price predictions are usually off by about $15,000.

+ **Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE)**: This tells us the size of the prediction error as a percentage of the real price. So instead of saying the model is off by $15,000, it might say it’s off by 5%. MAPE is useful when we're comparing predictions across properties with different price ranges.

+ **Prediction v.s. Actual Value Scatter Plot**: This is a chart that helps us see how close our model's predictions are to the actual sale prices. Each dot on the chart represents one property. If all the dots are near a straight diagonal line, it means the predictions are very close to the real prices. If they are scattered far away from that line, the model’s predictions are less accurate.

As a result, the **Random Forest model** shows the best performance, of which the price predictions are off by 34.02% ($214,118) on average.

```{r model_compare_data}
# Pull best hyperparam preds from out-of-fold predictions
lm_best_OOF_preds <- collect_predictions(lm_tuned) 

glmnet_best_OOF_preds <- collect_predictions(glmnet_tuned) %>% 
  filter(penalty  == glmnet_best_params$penalty[1] & mixture == glmnet_best_params$mixture[1])

rf_best_OOF_preds <- collect_predictions(rf_tuned) %>% 
  filter(mtry  == rf_best_params$mtry[1] & min_n == rf_best_params$min_n[1])

xgb_best_OOF_preds <- collect_predictions(xgb_tuned) %>% 
  filter(mtry  == xgb_best_params$mtry[1] & min_n == xgb_best_params$min_n[1])

# collect validation set predictions from last_fit model
lm_val_pred_geo     <- collect_predictions(lm_val_fit_geo)
glmnet_val_pred_geo <- collect_predictions(glmnet_val_fit_geo)
rf_val_pred_geo     <- collect_predictions(rf_val_fit_geo)
xgb_val_pred_geo    <- collect_predictions(xgb_val_fit_geo)


# Aggregate OOF predictions (they do not overlap with Validation prediction set)
OOF_preds <- rbind(data.frame(dplyr::select(lm_best_OOF_preds, .pred, log_adj_sale_price), model = "OLS"),
                   data.frame(dplyr::select(glmnet_best_OOF_preds, .pred, log_adj_sale_price), model = "RLS"),
                   data.frame(dplyr::select(rf_best_OOF_preds, .pred, log_adj_sale_price), model = "RF"),
                   data.frame(dplyr::select(xgb_best_OOF_preds, .pred, log_adj_sale_price), model = "XGB")) %>% 
  group_by(model) %>% 
  mutate(actual_price = exp(log_adj_sale_price) - 1,
         predicted_price = exp(.pred) - 1,
         RMSE = yardstick::rmse_vec(actual_price, predicted_price),
         MAE  = yardstick::mae_vec(actual_price, predicted_price),
         MAPE = mean(abs(predicted_price - actual_price) / actual_price)) %>% 
  ungroup() %>% 
  mutate(model = factor(model, levels=c("OLS","RLS","RF","XGB")))

# Aggregate predictions from Validation set
# improve MAPE
val_preds <- rbind(data.frame(lm_val_pred_geo, model = "OLS"),
                   data.frame(glmnet_val_pred_geo, model = "RLS"),
                   data.frame(rf_val_pred_geo, model = "RF"),
                   data.frame(xgb_val_pred_geo, model = "XGB")) %>% 
  left_join(., property_modeling %>% 
              rowid_to_column(var = ".row") %>% 
              dplyr::select(Latitude, Longitude, zoning_group, .row), 
            by = ".row") %>%
  group_by(model) %>%
  mutate(
    actual_price = exp(log_adj_sale_price) - 1,
    predicted_price = exp(.pred) - 1
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    RMSE = yardstick::rmse_vec(actual_price, predicted_price),
    MAE  = yardstick::mae_vec(actual_price, predicted_price),
    MAPE = mean(abs(predicted_price - actual_price) / actual_price)
  ) %>% 
  ungroup() %>% 
  mutate(model = factor(model, levels=c("OLS","RLS","RF","XGB")))
```

Putting the validation results of train and test set altogether, **Random Forest model shows the best and a stable performance among the four models**. Though the Regularized Linear Regression (RLS) model behaves well with a MAPE of 50.92%, it predicts 10% more error than the RF model, indicating a low level of stability. Within the test set, **the price predictions of the RF model are off by 32.32% ($222369.5) on average**, which is still a little high requiring further examination.

Predicted (in [orange]{style="color: #eb5600;"}) and observed (in [green]{style="color: #1a9988;"}) prices are compared by the scatter plots. The [orange]{style="color: #eb5600;"} and [green]{style="color: #1a9988;"} lines are closer in the RF model, indicating a better performance overall. However, the deviation suggests that, **on average, the model’s predictions are lower than the observed prices**. Examining the data points further reveals that prediction accuracy decreases as prices rise, confirming our concerns about the variability in the higher price ranges of the dataset. The intersection point suggests that our **RF model performs better for lower-valued housing prices around $422,857.5**.

### Random Forest Model

Out of 1,528 properties in the study area, **460** were used for model validation. Beyond assessing overall prediction error statistics, we further evaluated the Random Forest model’s generalizability across different spatial contexts and zoning categories. The results indicate generally strong performance, with **prediction errors below 30% for residential and mixed-use properties**. In particular, the model proves to be reliable and generalizable for scenario-based forecasting focused on zoning types such as **RMX3, CMX3, and CMX4**.

In the previous OLS model (Section 3.3.3.1), property price showed a strong relationship with zoning type, suggesting that **zoning serves as a meaningful proxy for how property value is perceived and regulated in practice**. For example, properties located in higher-density commercial zones such as CMX-4 or CMX-5 tended to exhibit significantly higher prices compared to those in residential zones like RM-1 or RSA-5. This reflects the **greater development potential and permitted uses in commercial mixed-use zones**, which typically allow for larger floor-area ratios (FAR), more flexible building types, and access to high-traffic areas—factors that increase market demand and drive up land value.

This pattern may also explain a preference for using the model’s predictions in future planning scenarios. Our random forest model shows high error rates in zones such as Unknown, SPPOA, CMX5, and IRMX, with some predictions exceeding four times the actual price. However, **it performs relatively well in RMX3, CMX3, and CMX4**, zones that are primarily residential or commercial mixed-use and are central to future zoning changes and community impact. While the model has an overall MAPE of 32%, its stronger performance in RMX and CMX zones suggests it is more reliable and generalizable for **scenario-based forecasting** focused on these zoning types.

Excluding industrial zones and high-rise office buildings from the analysis (IRMX, CMX5), the validation results show a MAPE of 30.82% and a MAE of $205080.1, representing **an improvement of approximately 4% points in error and a reduction of over $20,000 in average absolute deviation compared to the full-sample predictions**. This suggests that the model performs more accurately when focused on residential and mixed-use properties, which are more consistent in pricing patterns and better represented in the training data. In contrast, **industrial parcels and high-density commercial zones** like CMX5 often exhibit highly variable and site-specific values driven by factors such as floor-area bonuses, special-use permits, and redevelopment potential—factors that are **difficult to capture with general property features alone**.

```{r scenario 1 data processing, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, quiet=TRUE, results='hide'}
grocery <- readRDS("Dataset/poi/poi_grocery.rds")
res_poi <- readRDS("Dataset/poi/poi_restaurant.rds")

grocery_idx <- st_nearest_feature(property_proj, grocery_proj)
restaurant_idx <- st_nearest_feature(property_proj, restaurant_proj)

property_proj$nearest_grocery_name <- grocery_proj$name[grocery_idx]
property_proj$nearest_restaurant_name <- restaurant_proj$name[restaurant_idx]

property_proj$nearest_grocery_dist <- st_distance(property_proj, grocery_proj[grocery_idx, ], by_element = TRUE)
property_proj$nearest_restaurant_dist <- st_distance(property_proj, restaurant_proj[restaurant_idx, ], by_element = TRUE)

clean_property_poi_distances <- function(property_sf) {
  property_sf %>%
    mutate(
      nearest_grocery_dist_m = as.numeric(nearest_grocery_dist),
      nearest_restaurant_dist_m = as.numeric(nearest_restaurant_dist)
    ) %>%
    select(-nearest_grocery_dist, -nearest_restaurant_dist)
}

property1_final <- clean_property_poi_distances(property_proj)


calculate_nearest_distance <- function(set_points, other_layer) {
  nearest_idx <- st_nearest_feature(set_points, other_layer)
  st_distance(set_points, other_layer[nearest_idx, ], by_element = TRUE) %>% as.numeric()
}
```

```{r}
median_bedroom <- median(as.numeric(as.character(property_S1_no_fe$number_of_bedrooms)), na.rm = TRUE)
median_bathroom <- median(as.numeric(as.character(property_S1_no_fe$number_of_bathrooms)), na.rm = TRUE)

property_S1_fe <- property_S1_no_fe %>%
  filter(!zoning %in% c("I2", "SPPOA"))%>%
  mutate(
        # Neighborhood Name
    nhoods_name = case_when(
      nhoods_name %in% c("CENTER_CITY", "LOGAN_SQUARE") ~ "WEST_PART",
      TRUE ~ nhoods_name
    ),

    # Land Use
    landuse = case_when(
      landuse %in% c("Park/Open Space", "Other/Unknown", "Commercial Business/Professional") ~ "Open Space/Business",
      landuse %in% c("Commercial Consumer", "Commercial Mixed Residential",
                     "Industrial", "Transportation", "Culture/Amusement") ~ "Commercial",
      landuse %in% c("Civic/Institution", "Residential High") ~ "Residential High/Civic",
      TRUE ~ landuse
    ),
    # Year Built
    year_built = as.numeric(year_built),
    year_built_missing = ifelse(is.na(year_built), 1, 0),
    year_built_group = case_when(
       is.na(year_built) ~ "Unknown",
       year_built < 1940 ~ "Pre-War",
       year_built < 2000 ~ "Post-War Mid",
       year_built < 2020 ~ "Modern",
       year_built >= 2020 ~ "New"
    ),
    year_built_group = factor(year_built_group, levels = c("Pre-War", "Post-War Mid", "Modern", "New", "Unknown")),
    # Log Transforms
    log_price = log(sale_price),
    log_dist_highway = log(distance_to_I676 + 1),

    # Central Air
    central_air = case_when(
      central_air %in% c("Y", "1")  ~ "Y",
      central_air %in% c("N", "0") ~ "N",
      TRUE ~ "Unknown"
    ),
    central_air = factor(central_air),
    central_air_missing = ifelse(central_air == "Unknown", 1, 0),

    # Garage Spaces
    garage_spaces_missing = ifelse(is.na(garage_spaces), 1, 0),
    garage_spaces = case_when(
#      is.na(garage_spaces) ~ "Unknown",
      garage_spaces == 0 | garage_spaces == 1 ~ "less than 2",
      TRUE ~ "2 or more"
    ),
    garage_spaces = factor(garage_spaces),

    # Bedrooms
    number_of_bedrooms = as.numeric(as.character(number_of_bedrooms)),
    number_of_bedrooms_missing = ifelse(is.na(number_of_bedrooms), 1, 0),
    number_of_bedrooms_filled = ifelse(is.na(number_of_bedrooms), median_bedroom, number_of_bedrooms),
    number_of_bedrooms = case_when(
      is.na(number_of_bedrooms) ~ "Unknown",
      number_of_bedrooms == 0 ~ "0",
      number_of_bedrooms == 1 ~ "1",
      number_of_bedrooms %in% c(2, 3) ~ "2",
      number_of_bedrooms %in% c(5, 6) ~ "3",
      number_of_bedrooms == 4 ~"4",
      number_of_bedrooms %in% c(7, 9, 12) ~ "5"
    ),
    number_of_bedrooms = factor(number_of_bedrooms),

    # Bathrooms
    number_of_bathrooms = as.numeric(as.character(number_of_bathrooms)),
    number_of_bathrooms_missing = ifelse(is.na(number_of_bathrooms), 1, 0),
    number_of_bathrooms_filled = ifelse(is.na(number_of_bathrooms), median_bathroom, number_of_bathrooms),
    number_of_bathrooms = case_when(
      number_of_bathrooms == 0 ~ "0",
      number_of_bathrooms == 1 ~ "1",
      number_of_bathrooms == 2 ~ "2",
      number_of_bathrooms %in% c(3, 4, 5) ~ "3-5",
      number_of_bathrooms == 6 ~ "6",
      number_of_bathrooms == 7 ~ "7",
      TRUE ~ "Unknown"
    ),
    number_of_bathrooms = factor(number_of_bathrooms),

    # Total Livable Area
    total_livable_area = ifelse(is.na(total_livable_area) | total_livable_area == 1, 0, total_livable_area),

    # Quality Grade
    quality_grade = case_when(
      quality_grade %in% c("A ", "A-") | is.na(quality_grade) ~ "Good",
      quality_grade %in% c("3 ", "C+", "C")  ~ "Average",
      TRUE ~ "Below Average"
    ),
    quality_grade = factor(quality_grade, levels = c("Good", "Average", "Below Average")),
    quality_grade_missing = ifelse(is.na(quality_grade), 1, 0),

    # Construction
    general_construction = as.character(general_construction),
    general_construction = case_when(
      is.na(general_construction) ~ "Unknown",
      TRUE ~ general_construction
    ),
    general_construction = factor(general_construction),
    general_construction_missing = ifelse(general_construction == "Unknown", 1, 0),

    # Separate Utilities
    separate_utilities = case_when(
      is.na(separate_utilities) ~ "Unknown",
      TRUE ~ separate_utilities
    ),
    separate_utilities = factor(separate_utilities, levels = c("A", "B", "C", "Unknown")),
    separate_utilities_missing = ifelse(separate_utilities == "Unknown", 1, 0),

    # Exterior Condition
    exterior_condition = case_when(
      exterior_condition == 2 | is.na(exterior_condition)~ "Average",
      exterior_condition %in% c(1, 6, 7)  ~ "Good",
      exterior_condition %in% c(3, 4, 5) ~ "Below Average"
 #     TRUE ~ "Unknown"
    ),
    exterior_condition = factor(exterior_condition),

    # Interior Condition
    interior_condition = case_when(
      interior_condition %in% c(1,6) ~ "Good",
      is.na(interior_condition) | interior_condition %in% c(2, 5, 7) ~ "Average",
      interior_condition %in% c(3, 4, 5, 6) ~ "Below Average",
      TRUE ~ "Unknown"
    ),
    interior_condition = factor(interior_condition),
    # Category Code
    category_code_original = as.character(category_code),
    category_code_group = case_when(
      category_code == "12" ~ "6 ",
      category_code == "14" ~ "2 ",
      category_code == "10" ~ "4 ",
      category_code == "15" ~ "5 ",
      category_code == "16" ~ "4 ",
      category_code == "7 "  ~ "4 ",
      category_code == "8 "  ~ "6 ",
      category_code == "9 "  ~ "2 ",
      category_code %in% c("1 ", "2 ", "3 ", "4 ", "5 ", "6 ") ~ category_code,
      TRUE ~ "Other"
    ),
    category_code = factor(category_code_group),

    # Zoning
    zoning_group = case_when(
      zoning %in% c("CMX5") ~ "CMX5",
      zoning %in% c("IRMX") ~ "IRMX",
      zoning %in% c("RM1", "RM2", "RM4") ~ "RM",
      zoning %in% c("RMX3") ~ "RMX3",
      zoning %in% c("RSA5") ~ "RSA5",
      zoning %in% c("ICMX") ~ "ICMX",
      zoning %in% c("CMX2.5", "CMX2", "CMX1") ~ "CMX(1,2,2.5)",
      zoning %in% c("CMX3", "CMX4") ~ "CMX(3,4)",
      TRUE ~ "Other"
    ),
    zoning_group = factor(zoning_group),

    zoning = case_when(
      is.na(zoning) ~ "Unknown",
      TRUE ~ zoning
    ),
    zoning = factor(zoning),
    zip_code = factor(zip_code)
  )
```

<span style="color: #eb5600;"><b>Scenario 0. Where We Start: The I-676 Highway as a Barrier</b></span>  

- Highway remains a physical and economic barrier, dividing Chinatown and limiting connectivity.  
- Property values show spatial imbalance — sale prices increase significantly with distance from I-676 on the <span style="color: #1a9988;"><b>south side</b></span>, but decline with distance on the <span style="color: #eb5600;"><b>north side</b></span>.  
- Reinforces unequal development patterns, with opportunity concentrated in the south and disinvestment in the north.  
- No intervention means no shift in trajectory — existing fragmentation and disparity persist as the baseline.  

<span style="color: #1a9988;"><b>Scenario 1. A First Step: Capping I-676 to Reconnect Chinatown</b></span>  

- One cap serves as a Cap Park, while two others reconnect streets and improve circulation across the highway.  
- Restores physical connections between north and south Chinatown, enhancing walkability and spatial continuity.  
- Helps stabilize fragmented property values, narrowing the north–south gap, though overall price growth remains limited without land use changes.  
- Signals future reinvestment potential, but remains a modest intervention in the absence of structural development policies.

<span style="color: #a66bbe;"><b>Scenario 2. Turning Connection into Growth: Cap Park + Alternate Zoning / Land Use</b></span>  

- Building upon Scenario 1, Scenario 2 integrates both park infrastructure and zoning interventions to unlock the full development potential of underutilized parcels.  
- <span style="color: #eb5600;">Under the commercial perspective, part of **Vacant Land & Industrial Properties** are converted into **Commercial Mixed-Use developments**.</span>  
- <span style="color: #eb5600;">Under the residential perspective, part of **Vacant Land & Single-Family Properties** are converted into **Multi-Family Properties** or **Commercial Mixed-Use developments**.</span>  
- It combines highway cap infrastructure with strategic zoning and land use changes across both sides of I-676.  
- Under the commercial perspective, reclassify part of vacant and industrial parcels as commercial or commercial–mixed-use properties, supporting walkable retail and local services.  
- Under the residential perspective, reclassify part of Single-Family residential and vacant lots as Multi-Family, expanding affordable housing options and increasing population capacity.  
- These combined interventions unlock more development value and lead to significant property price increases, especially where zoning changes align with better access and street connectivity. However, while the south shows notable value increases, the north continues to lag, reflecting persistent structural challenges that require further public investment in amenities and infrastructure.

```{r S2_comm -FE countinued , quiet=TRUE, results='hide'}
      number_of_bathrooms == 6 ~ "6",
      number_of_bathrooms == 7 ~ "7",
      TRUE ~ "Unknown"
    ),
    number_of_bathrooms = factor(number_of_bathrooms),

    # Total Livable Area
    total_livable_area = ifelse(is.na(total_livable_area) | total_livable_area == 1, 0, total_livable_area),

    # Quality Grade
    quality_grade = case_when(
      quality_grade %in% c("A ", "A-") | is.na(quality_grade) ~ "Good",
      quality_grade %in% c("3 ", "C+", "C")  ~ "Average",
      TRUE ~ "Below Average"
    ),
    quality_grade = factor(quality_grade, levels = c("Good", "Average", "Below Average")),
    quality_grade_missing = ifelse(is.na(quality_grade), 1, 0),

    # Construction
    general_construction = as.character(general_construction),
    general_construction = case_when(
      is.na(general_construction) ~ "Unknown",

    ),

    general_construction_missing = ifelse(general_construction == "Unknown", 1, 0),

    # Separate Utilities

    ),
    separate_utilities = factor(separate_utilities, levels = c("A", "B", "C", "Unknown")),
    separate_utilities_missing = ifelse(separate_utilities == "Unknown", 1, 0),

    # Exterior Condition
    exterior_condition = case_when(
      exterior_condition == 2 | is.na(exterior_condition)~ "Average",
      exterior_condition %in% c(1, 6, 7)  ~ "Good",
      exterior_condition %in% c(3, 4, 5) ~ "Below Average"
 #     TRUE ~ "Unknown"
    ),
    exterior_condition = factor(exterior_condition),

    # Interior Condition
    interior_condition = case_when(
      interior_condition %in% c(1,6) ~ "Good",
      is.na(interior_condition) | interior_condition %in% c(2, 5, 7) ~ "Average",
      interior_condition %in% c(3, 4, 5, 6) ~ "Below Average",
      TRUE ~ "Unknown"
    ),
    interior_condition = factor(interior_condition),

    # Category Code
    category_code_original = as.character(category_code),
    category_code_group = case_when(
      category_code == "12" ~ "6 ",
      category_code == "14" ~ "2 ",
      category_code == "10" ~ "4 ",
      category_code == "15" ~ "5 ",
      category_code == "16" ~ "4 ",
      category_code == "7 "  ~ "4 ",
      category_code == "8 "  ~ "6 ",
      category_code == "9 "  ~ "2 ",
      category_code %in% c("1 ", "2 ", "3 ", "4 ", "5 ", "6 ") ~ category_code,
      TRUE ~ "Other"
    ),
    category_code = factor(category_code_group),

    # Zoning
    zoning_group = case_when(
      zoning %in% c("CMX5") ~ "CMX5",
      zoning %in% c("IRMX") ~ "IRMX",
      zoning %in% c("RM1", "RM2", "RM4") ~ "RM",
      zoning %in% c("RMX3") ~ "RMX3",
      zoning %in% c("RSA5") ~ "RSA5",
      zoning %in% c("ICMX") ~ "ICMX",
      zoning %in% c("SPPOA") ~ "SPPOA",
      zoning %in% c("I2") ~ "I2",
      zoning %in% c("CMX2.5", "CMX2", "CMX1") ~ "CMX(1,2,2.5)",
      zoning %in% c("CMX3", "CMX4") ~ "CMX(3,4)",
      TRUE ~ "Other"
    ),
    zoning_group = factor(zoning_group),

    zoning = case_when(
      is.na(zoning) ~ "Unknown",
      TRUE ~ zoning
    ),
    zoning = factor(zoning),
    zip_code = factor(zip_code)
  )
```

```{r S2 - comm -res, fig.height=5, fig.width=12, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# S2 changed
property_S2_comm <- property_S2_fe %>%
  filter(
    landuse_old != landuse_new |

  )

S2_changed_map <- ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = studyarea, fill = "transparent", color = "grey60", linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 1.2) +
  geom_sf(data = discontinuity, fill = "black", color = "transparent") +
  geom_sf(data = Chinatown_Stitch %>% filter(FID_ == 500391), fill = "grey", color = "grey", linewidth = 1) +
  geom_sf(data = Chinatown_Stitch %>% filter(FID_ != 500391), fill = "white", color = "grey", linewidth = 1) +
  
  geom_sf(data = property_S2_comm %>% filter(!is.na(predicted_price)), 
          aes(colour = cut(predicted_price, breaks = qBr_S1, labels = qBr_S1_labels, include.lowest = TRUE)),
          show.legend = "point", size = 0.8) +

  scale_colour_manual(

    breaks = qBr_S1_labels,
    labels = qBr_S1_labels,
    name = "Predicted Sale Price"
  ) +
  guides(color = guide_legend(override.aes = list(size = 3))) +

  theme_void() +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(size = 18, face = "bold",hjust = 0.5),

  )
```

```{r S2- data wrangling - FE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, quiet=TRUE, results='hide'}
      is.na(general_construction) ~ "Unknown",
      TRUE ~ general_construction
    ),
    general_construction = factor(general_construction),
    general_construction_missing = ifelse(general_construction == "Unknown", 1, 0),

    # Separate Utilities
    separate_utilities = case_when(
      is.na(separate_utilities) ~ "Unknown",
      TRUE ~ separate_utilities
    ),
    separate_utilities = factor(separate_utilities, levels = c("A", "B", "C", "Unknown")),
    separate_utilities_missing = ifelse(separate_utilities == "Unknown", 1, 0),

    # Exterior Condition
    exterior_condition = case_when(
      exterior_condition == 2 | is.na(exterior_condition)~ "Average",
      exterior_condition %in% c(1, 6, 7)  ~ "Good",
      exterior_condition %in% c(3, 4, 5) ~ "Below Average"
 #     TRUE ~ "Unknown"
    ),
    exterior_condition = factor(exterior_condition),

    # Interior Condition
    interior_condition = case_when(
      interior_condition %in% c(1,6) ~ "Good",
      is.na(interior_condition) | interior_condition %in% c(2, 5, 7) ~ "Average",
      interior_condition %in% c(3, 4, 5, 6) ~ "Below Average",
      TRUE ~ "Unknown"
    ),
    interior_condition = factor(interior_condition),

    # Category Code
    category_code_original = as.character(category_code),
    category_code_group = case_when(
      category_code == "12" ~ "6 ",
      category_code == "14" ~ "2 ",
      category_code == "10" ~ "4 ",
      category_code == "15" ~ "5 ",
      category_code == "16" ~ "4 ",
      category_code == "7 "  ~ "4 ",
      category_code == "8 "  ~ "6 ",
      category_code == "9 "  ~ "2 ",
      category_code %in% c("1 ", "2 ", "3 ", "4 ", "5 ", "6 ") ~ category_code,
      TRUE ~ "Other"
    ),
    category_code = factor(category_code_group),

    # Zoning
    zoning_group = case_when(
      zoning %in% c("CMX5") ~ "CMX5",
      zoning %in% c("IRMX") ~ "IRMX",
      zoning %in% c("RM1", "RM2", "RM4") ~ "RM",
      zoning %in% c("RMX3") ~ "RMX3",
      zoning %in% c("RSA5") ~ "RSA5",
      zoning %in% c("ICMX") ~ "ICMX",
      zoning %in% c("SPPOA") ~ "SPPOA",
      zoning %in% c("I2") ~ "I2",
      zoning %in% c("CMX2.5", "CMX2", "CMX1") ~ "CMX(1,2,2.5)",
      zoning %in% c("CMX3", "CMX4") ~ "CMX(3,4)",
      TRUE ~ "Other"
    ),
    zoning_group = factor(zoning_group),

    zoning = case_when(
      is.na(zoning) ~ "Unknown",
      TRUE ~ zoning
    ),
    zoning = factor(zoning),
    zip_code = factor(zip_code)
  )
```


## Scenarios Exploration
### Median Property Value  
**South side price increases across interventions** is first evidenced in the shift of median values.  
From <span style="color: #eb5600;"><b>Scenario 0</b></span> to <span style="color: #a66bbe;"><b>Scenario 2</b></span>, the median price increases from <span style="color: #eb5600;"><b>$402,561</b></span>
to <span style="color: #1a9988;"><b>$438,338</b></span> in <span style="color: #1a9988;"><b>Scenario 1</b></span>, and further to <span style="color: #a66bbe;"><b>$487,683</b></span> in <span style="color: #a66bbe;"><b>Scenario 2</b></span>.  

This progressive shift aligns with the intervention logic:  
- <span style="color: #1a9988;"><b>Scenario 1</b></span> introduces physical reconnection through caps, producing moderate price uplift.  
- <span style="color: #a66bbe;"><b>Scenario 2</b></span> builds upon this with zoning reform, pushing the distribution further rightward.  

These results suggest that each layer of intervention contributes incrementally to value change. Physical improvements alone offer moderate benefits, while combining them with zoning changes leads to stronger price increases.

### Discontinuity Across I-676  
To further quantify highway-related land value effects for each scenario, we build on the discontinuity analysis by estimating price changes at varying distances from the highway, controlling for side-specific spatial patterns.  

We fit separate log-linear models for the north and south using sale prices (or predicted prices under each scenario), regressing `log price` on `log distance to highway`, respectively.  

For comparability, we apply a baseline distance of 50 meters from the highway and compute price changes at 100m, 150m, and 200m, relative to that baseline.  

Based on the highway effect analysis in the previous section, we focus our interpretation on the **150-meter** distance, which captures the clearest divergence in pricing behavior across sides and scenarios.

<h4><b>Scenario 0</b></h4>  

Without intervention, I-676 remains a strong physical and economic barrier dividing the north and south. The discontinuity effect is clearly observed in the price-distance relationship:  

- **South Side**: Property values increase significantly with distance from the highway. At 150m, prices are approximately $328,943 higher (+50.6%) than at 50m. This suggests a strong negative externality from proximity to the highway, especially on the south side.  
- **North Side**: Prices decrease slightly with distance. At 150m, the decline is $19,051 (–2.9%), indicating structural constraints that prevent price growth, despite increased distance.  
- **Overall**: The average change across both sides shows a $108,693 increase (+16.6%), but this masks growing spatial inequality between the two areas.  

Without policy intervention, market behavior reinforces existing inequalities: properties on the south side benefit from distancing, while the north remains stagnant.

```{r}
get_price_change_full <- function(data, price_col, scenario_label, distances = seq(50, 200, by = 50), baseline_price = 650000) {
  data_all <- data %>%
    mutate(dist_model = abs(distance_to_highway)) %>%
    filter(!is.na(!!sym(price_col)), !is.na(distance_to_highway))

  formula_all   <- as.formula(paste0("log(", price_col, " + 1) ~ log(dist_model + 1)"))
  formula_south <- as.formula(paste0("log(", price_col, " + 1) ~ log(abs(distance_to_highway) + 1)"))
  formula_north <- as.formula(paste0("log(", price_col, " + 1) ~ distance_to_highway"))

  lm_all   <- lm(formula_all,   data = data_all)
  lm_south <- lm(formula_south, data = data_all %>% filter(I676_NS == "south"))
  lm_north <- lm(formula_north, data = data_all %>% filter(I676_NS == "north"))

  baseline_log_all   <- predict(lm_all,   newdata = data.frame(dist_model = 50))
  baseline_log_south <- predict(lm_south, newdata = data.frame(distance_to_highway = 50))
  baseline_log_north <- predict(lm_north, newdata = data.frame(distance_to_highway = 50))

  pred_log_all   <- predict(lm_all,   newdata = data.frame(dist_model = distances))
  pred_log_south <- predict(lm_south, newdata = data.frame(distance_to_highway = distances))
  pred_log_north <- predict(lm_north, newdata = data.frame(distance_to_highway = distances))

  price_est_all   <- baseline_price * exp(pred_log_all - baseline_log_all)
  price_est_south <- baseline_price * exp(pred_log_south - baseline_log_south)
  price_est_north <- baseline_price * exp(pred_log_north - baseline_log_north)

  tibble(
    Scenario            = scenario_label,
    Distance_m          = distances,
    South_Change        = round(price_est_south - baseline_price),
    North_Change        = round(price_est_north - baseline_price),
    Overall_Change      = round(price_est_all - baseline_price),
    South_Change_Pct    = round((price_est_south - baseline_price) / baseline_price * 100, 1),
    North_Change_Pct    = round((price_est_north - baseline_price) / baseline_price * 100, 1),
    Overall_Change_Pct  = round((price_est_all - baseline_price) / baseline_price * 100, 1)
  )
}
S0_table <- get_price_change_full(discontinuity_S0, "adj_sale_price", "Scenario 0")

S0_table %>%
  kable("html", caption = "Price Change (Amount and %) from 50m Baseline — Scenario 0") %>%
  kable_styling(full_width = FALSE, bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed")) %>%
  row_spec(0, bold = TRUE, background = "#1a9988", color = "white") %>%
  row_spec(which(S0_table$Distance_m == 150), background = "#eb5600", color = "white")
```

<h4><b>Scenario 1</b></h4>

- **South Side**: Prices continue to increase with distance, showing a $176,934 increase (+27.2%) at 150m. The growth is slightly less than in Scenario 0, possibly due to reduced marginal benefits from improved connectivity alone.  
- **North Side**: Although prices still decrease, the decline is less sharp—$5,738 (–1.1%)—indicating slight improvements from better access, though not enough to reverse the decreasing trend.  
- **Overall**: Prices increase by $98,378 (+15.0%) at 150m. The effects are more balanced, but limited by unchanged zoning. Cap installation helps moderate the highway’s barrier effect. It leads to healthier price growth on the south side and reduces losses on the north, but cannot fully address market asymmetries without further zoning or other policy supports.

<h4><b>Scenario 2</b></h4>

- **South Side**: Property values increase by $194,111 (+29.9%) at 150m, slightly higher than in Scenario 1. This growth reflects increased development potential under new land uses, especially when combined with improved connectivity. However, these are modeled outcomes based on full policy implementation; they do not reflect current market behavior, but a future in which land use changes are realized and development responds accordingly.  
- **North Side**: Prices still decrease slightly (–$20,222, –3.1%). Despite land use adjustments, the north side may continue to face structural disadvantages—such as lower demand, inferior connectivity, or market perception—which limit the effectiveness of zoning reform alone.  
- **Overall**: Price increases across both sides are more evenly distributed than in Scenario 0, but the total gain ($87,290, +13.4%) is lower than in other scenarios. This suggests that regulatory changes alone, while valuable, require complementary investments and broader planning efforts to fully realize their benefits.

### Price Change Patterns

<h4>**Scenario 0 vs. Scenario 1**</h4>  
Compared to Scenario 0, Scenario 1 produces a notable shift in spatial price patterns, especially on the south side of I-676:  

**South Side**: A wide cluster of parcels shows 10–50% price increases, especially within and surrounding the Stitch area. Several parcels directly adjacent to the cap park even exceed 200%, indicating strong responsiveness to improved connectivity. This confirms the earlier discontinuity plot finding: south-side values increase with distance from the highway due to strong pre-existing disamenity.  

**North Side**: While less dramatic, we observe several parcels—especially those not adjacent to the highway—also showing moderate increases (10–50%). Some parcels even exceed 100%, suggesting that building cap park does provide benefit across both sides, albeit to different extents.  

**Overall**: The price improvement is not localized to the cap. We see dispersed growth across Chinatown and the Callowhill area, particularly where physical barriers were reduced. This contrasts with the limited north-side growth seen in Scenario 0. These patterns suggest that even without zoning reform, physical reconnection alone can unlock latent value, particularly for previously disconnected parcels. Again, proximity to the highway continues to shape the magnitude of price change.
```{r message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
property_S1_perc_change <- property_S1_predict%>%
  filter(!is.na(adj_sale_price), adj_sale_price > 100) %>%
  mutate(
    perc_change = round((predicted_price - adj_sale_price) / adj_sale_price * 100, 1),
    perc_bucket = case_when(
      perc_change < -10  ~ "< -10%",
      perc_change < 0    ~ "-10% to 0%",
      perc_change < 10   ~ "0% to +10%",
      perc_change < 50   ~ "+10% to +50%",
      perc_change < 100  ~ "+50 % to +100%",
      perc_change < 200  ~ "+100% to +200%",
      TRUE               ~ "> 200%"
    ),
    perc_bucket = factor(perc_bucket,
                         levels = c("< -10%", "-10% to 0%", "0% to +10%",
                                    "+10% to +50%","+50 % to +100%", "+100% to +200%", "> 200%")),
    size_bucket = case_when(
      perc_bucket == "< -10%"        ~ 1.5,
      perc_bucket == "-10% to 0%"    ~ 2,
      perc_bucket == "0% to +10%"    ~ 2.5,
      perc_bucket == "+10% to +50%"  ~ 4,
      perc_bucket == "+50 % to +100%" ~ 5,
      perc_bucket == "+50% to +200%" ~ 6,
      perc_bucket == "> 200%"        ~ 7
    ),
    property_category = case_when(
      category_code_chain %in% c("3:Mixed Use", "4:Commercial") ~ "Commercial",
      category_code_chain %in% c("1:Single Family", "2:Multi Family", "14:Apartments > 4 units") ~ "Residential",
      category_code_chain == "15:Retail" ~ "Retail",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(property_category)) %>%
  mutate(property_category = factor(property_category, levels = c("Commercial", "Residential", "Retail"))) %>%
  select(
    parcel_number, objectid, perc_change, perc_bucket, size_bucket, geometry,
    predicted_price, zoning, category_code, landuse, property_category, everything()
  )
```

<h4>**Scenario 1 vs. Scenario 2**</h4>  

**South Side**: Compared with Scenario 1, Scenario 2 shows more pronounced price growth on the south side, particularly around the core Stitch parcels and the park cap area. These parcels already showed moderate appreciation under Scenario 1, but values rose further under Scenario 2, consistent with added development capacity modeled in zoning reform.  

**North Side**: On the north side, a different pattern emerges. Though overall price response remains limited, the few parcels with significant increases are primarily located farther from the highway, especially in the northeastern corner. This suggests that even where zoning enables new use types, proximity to the highway still limits value recovery. Distance from I-676 remains a major spatial determinant of appreciation potential.  

**Overall**: These contrasting patterns reinforce earlier discontinuity results: the south side gains from both physical reconnection and policy-driven densification, whereas the north side remains constrained by structural disadvantages and weak location fundamentals, even with the same zoning changes applied.
```{r message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
property_S2_perc_change <- property_S4_predict %>%
  filter(!is.na(adj_sale_price), adj_sale_price > 100) %>%
  mutate(
    perc_change = round((predicted_price - adj_sale_price) / adj_sale_price * 100, 1),
    perc_bucket = case_when(
      perc_change < -10  ~ "< -10%",
      perc_change < 0    ~ "-10% to 0%",
      perc_change < 10   ~ "0% to +10%",
      perc_change < 50   ~ "+10% to +50%",
      perc_change < 100  ~ "+50 % to +100%",
      perc_change < 200  ~ "+100% to +200%",
      TRUE               ~ "> 200%"
    ),
    perc_bucket = factor(perc_bucket,
                         levels = c("< -10%", "-10% to 0%", "0% to +10%",
                                    "+10% to +50%", "+50 % to +100%", "+100% to +200%", "> 200%")),
    size_bucket = case_when(
      perc_bucket == "< -10%"         ~ 1.5,
      perc_bucket == "-10% to 0%"     ~ 2,
      perc_bucket == "0% to +10%"     ~ 2.5,
      perc_bucket == "+10% to +50%"   ~ 4,
      perc_bucket == "+50 % to +100%" ~ 5,
      perc_bucket == "+50% to +200%"  ~ 6,
      perc_bucket == "> 200%"         ~ 7
    ),
    property_category = case_when(
      category_code_chain %in% c("3:Mixed Use", "4:Commercial") ~ "Commercial",
      category_code_chain %in% c("1:Single Family", "2:Multi Family", "14:Apartments > 4 units") ~ "Residential",
      category_code_chain == "15:Retail" ~ "Retail",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(property_category)) %>%
  mutate(property_category = factor(property_category, levels = c("Commercial", "Residential", "Retail"))) %>%
  select(
    parcel_number, objectid, perc_change, perc_bucket, size_bucket, property_category, geometry,
    predicted_price, zoning, category_code, landuse, everything()
  )
property_S1_perc_change <- st_transform(property_S1_perc_change, 4326)
property_S2_perc_change <- st_transform(property_S2_perc_change, 4326)
price_change_s1s2 <- property_S1_perc_change %>%
  filter(!is.na(adj_sale_price), adj_sale_price > 100) %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%
  select(objectid, predicted_price_s1 = predicted_price) %>%
  inner_join(
    property_S2_perc_change %>%
      select(objectid, parcel_number, location, landuse, category_code, zoning, geometry, predicted_price_s2 = predicted_price), #alternate 
    by = "objectid"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    perc_change = round((predicted_price_s2 - predicted_price_s1) / predicted_price_s1 * 100, 1),
    perc_bucket = case_when(
      perc_change < 0               ~ "< 0%",
      perc_change == 0              ~ "0%",
      perc_change <= 10             ~ "0–10%",
      perc_change <= 20             ~ "10–20%",
      perc_change <= 30             ~ "20–30%",
      perc_change <= 50             ~ "30–50%",
      TRUE                          ~ "> 50%"
    ),
    perc_bucket = factor(perc_bucket,
                         levels = c("< 0%", "0%", "0–10%", "10–20%", "20–30%", "30–50%", "> 50%")),
    size_bucket = case_when(
      perc_bucket == "< 0%"     ~ 2,
      perc_bucket == "0%"       ~ 2.5,
      perc_bucket == "0–10%"    ~ 3,
      perc_bucket == "10–20%"   ~ 4,
      perc_bucket == "20–30%"   ~ 5,
      perc_bucket == "30–50%"   ~ 6,
      perc_bucket == "> 50%"    ~ 7
    )
  ) %>%
  st_as_sf(sf_column_name = "geometry",crs = 4326) %>%
  st_transform(4326)
```

# Recommendations

<h5><b>1. Target development toward parcels with strong market signals</b></h5>

In both <span style="color: #1a9988;"><b>Scenario 1</b></span> and <span style="color: #a66bbe;"><b>Scenario 2</b></span>, our modeling shows that south-side parcels, especially those adjacent to the park cap and close to I-676, experienced substantial price increases. The discontinuity plots reveal a positive correlation between greater distance from I-676 and property values on the south side. This is further supported by the percentage change maps, where many parcels increased by over <b>50%</b>, with some exceeding <b>200%</b>. These patterns suggest that these parcels already meet key feasibility conditions, and current market signals support their potential for more intensive land use.

We recommend OTIS prioritize investment, densification, and infrastructure support in these high-potential areas. This approach ensures that new development occurs where the market is already active, reducing risk of displacement by reinforcing value where it is already rising.

<h5><b>2. Reevaluate underutilized areas by assessing capacity and constraints</b></h5>

<span style="color: #a66bbe;"><b>Scenario 2</b></span> reveals that land use adjustments alone are insufficient to generate price increases on the north side comparable to those observed on the south side. Despite zoning changes, parcels adjacent to the highway continued to experience price decreases. This is confirmed by the discontinuity plots, which show a persistently negative slope. However, several parcel clusters located farther from I-676 present price increases, suggesting spatial variation in how parcels respond to zoning changes.

This suggests that underutilized areas require more than regulatory change. OTIS should consider physical access, transit connectivity, and infrastructure readiness before promoting development in these zones. Without addressing these baseline constraints, rezoning may not yield equitable or effective results.

<h5><b>3. Align zoning changes with implementation checks</b></h5>

Our scenario-based price change evaluation, using a <b>150-meter</b> baseline, shows clear divergence in responsiveness across the highway divide, suggesting underlying differences in market readiness and infrastructure.

Therefore, OTIS should conduct feasibility checks before rezoning, considering each site’s current use, infrastructure, surrounding parcel dynamics, and market demand. This avoids speculative mismatches and ensures zoning reforms translate into actionable and equitable development when implementing the Stitch project.

<h5><b>4. Strengthen monitoring mechanisms for equity</b></h5>

Median property prices increase significantly from <b>~$402,000</b> in <span style="color: #eb5600;"><b>Scenario 0</b></span> to <b>~$488,000</b> in <span style="color: #a66bbe;"><b>Scenario 2</b></span>. These increases were spatially concentrated, particularly on the two sides.

We recommend OTIS monitor these trends closely. Parcels with large increases should be flagged for early intervention through affordability protections or land value stabilization tools. Simultaneously, parcels with slow or negative growth should be prioritized for supportive investment to prevent missed development opportunity across the corridor.

<span style="color: #eb5600; font-size: 20px;"><b>Conclusions</b></span>

In summary, the four recommendations we propose are not simply about promoting higher density or maximizing property value. They are grounded in spatial pattern recognition, identifying where development potential exists and where structural constraints persist.

The goal is to provide OTIS with a framework for advancing the Chinatown Stitch project while reminding OTIS to manage the market pressures that come with property value changes, so that sale price increase does not become a driver of displacement in the Chinatown community.

For areas where property values are already increasing, we emphasize that development efforts should be built on real and measurable feasibility. This means considering not only zoning adjustments but also the actual conditions of each site, including infrastructure capacity and the ability of the surrounding community to absorb change.

In areas where performance is weaker or conditions are less favorable, unlocking value will require improvements in infrastructure and the provision of essential public services. These areas should not be approached with investment decisions that rely only on projected value increases.

We also encourage OTIS to use property value changes as an early signal to guide housing policy. By establishing a mechanism to monitor and track areas that are sensitive to displacement risk, the city can respond proactively and prevent market-led redevelopment from becoming harmful.

By combining these strategies, city planners and policymakers can pursue a balanced path that advances physical reconnection and zoning changes while also preserving housing stability and long-term community presence in Chinatown.

```{r,eval=FALSE}
### Study Area Scale Anlysis
# Clean CPI data: format to monthly CPI series for inflation adjustment
colnames(cpi_data) <- c("half1", "half2", "cpi_date")
cpi_long <- cpi_data %>%
  mutate(
    Jan = `half1`, Feb = `half1`, Mar = `half1`, Apr = `half1`, May = `half1`, Jun = `half1`,
    Jul = `half2`, Aug = `half2`, Sep = `half2`, Oct = `half2`, Nov = `half2`, Dec = `half2`
  ) %>%
  select(-half1, -half2) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = -cpi_date, names_to = "Month", values_to = "CPI") %>%
  mutate(
    Month = match(Month, month.abb),
    date = as.Date(paste(cpi_date, Month, "01", sep = "-"))  
  ) %>%
  select(date, CPI)

# Clean citywide property data for inflation-adjusted sale price
property_philly <- property %>%
  mutate(sale_date = as.Date(sale_date, format = "%Y-%m-%d")) %>%
  filter(sale_date >= as.Date("2020-01-01") & sale_date <= as.Date("2024-12-31")) %>%
  filter(!is.na(sale_price), !is.na(total_livable_area)) %>%
  mutate(sale_month = floor_date(sale_date, "month")) %>%
  left_join(cpi_long, by = c("sale_month" = "date")) %>%
  mutate(CPI = as.numeric(CPI)) %>%
  mutate(adj_sale_price = sale_price * (340.331 / CPI)) %>%
  select(-sale_month, -recording_date, -other_building, 
         -assessment_date, -mailing_address_2, mailing_city_state, mailing_care_of)

# Remove extreme outliers using 5th and 95th percentiles
price_filtered_philly <- property_philly %>%
  filter(adj_sale_price >= 100)
q_philly <- quantile(price_filtered_philly$adj_sale_price, probs = c(0.05, 0.95), na.rm = TRUE)

property_philly2 <- property_philly %>%
  filter(adj_sale_price >= q_philly[1], adj_sale_price <= q_philly[2])

# Set CRS to projected EPSG:2272 for citywide data
property_philly <- st_transform(property_philly2, crs = 2272)

# Subset study area parcels using spatial intersection
property_studyarea <- st_intersection(property, studyarea)

# Clean study area property data and inflation-adjust prices
colnames(cpi_data) <- c("half1", "half2", "cpi_date")
cpi_long <- cpi_data %>%
  mutate(
    Jan = `half1`, Feb = `half1`, Mar = `half1`, Apr = `half1`, May = `half1`, Jun = `half1`,
    Jul = `half2`, Aug = `half2`, Sep = `half2`, Oct = `half2`, Nov = `half2`, Dec = `half2`
  ) %>%
  select(-half1, -half2) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = -cpi_date, names_to = "Month", values_to = "CPI") %>%
  mutate(
    Month = match(Month, month.abb),
    date = as.Date(paste(cpi_date, Month, "01", sep = "-"))  
  ) %>%
  select(date, CPI)

property_data <- property_studyarea %>%
  mutate(sale_date = as.Date(sale_date, format = "%Y-%m-%d")) %>%
  filter(!is.na(sale_price)) %>%
  filter(sale_date <= as.Date("2024-12-31")) %>%
  mutate(sale_month = floor_date(sale_date, "month")) %>%
  left_join(cpi_long, by = c("sale_month" = "date")) %>%
  mutate(CPI = as.numeric(CPI)) %>%
  mutate(adj_sale_price = sale_price * (340.331 / CPI)) %>%
  select(-sale_month, -recording_date, -other_building, 
         -assessment_date, -mailing_address_2, mailing_city_state, mailing_care_of, -state_code) %>%
  relocate(adj_sale_price, sale_price, .after = 2)

# Filter to 5th–95th percentile range of adjusted prices in study area
price_filtered <- property_data %>%
  filter(adj_sale_price >= 100)
q <- quantile(price_filtered$adj_sale_price, probs = c(0.05, 0.95), na.rm = TRUE)

property_data2 <- property_data %>%
  filter(adj_sale_price >= q[1], adj_sale_price <= q[2])

# Set CRS and tag parcels with highway side (north/south)
property1 <- st_transform(property_data2, crs = 2272)
property1 <- rbind(
  property1 %>% st_intersection(studyarea_north["geometry"]) %>%
    mutate(I676_NS = "north"),
  property1 %>% st_intersection(studyarea_south["geometry"]) %>%
    mutate(I676_NS = "south")
)

# Create clipped neighborhood layer for study area
nhood1 <- st_intersection(nhood, studyarea)

# Reorder zoning field and prioritize custom overrides
property1 <- property1 %>%
  select(1:2, zoning, location, everything()) %>%
  mutate(zoning = case_when(
    location == "1310-16 VINE ST" ~ "CMX4",   
    location == "252-56 N 13TH ST" ~ "CMX4",
    location == "255-57 N BROAD ST" ~ "CMX4",
    location == "451 N 12TH ST" ~ "CMX3",
    location == "453 N 12TH ST" ~ "CMX3",
    location == "447 N 12TH ST" ~ "CMX3",
    location == "1108 BUTTONWOOD ST" ~ "CMX3",
    location == "1104 BUTTONWOOD ST" ~ "CMX3",
    location == "256-60 N MARVINE ST" ~ "CMX4",
    location == "820 VINE ST" ~ "CMX4",
    TRUE ~ zoning
  ))

# Manually override central air presence where known
target_locations_N <- c(
  "1232 SUMMER ST", 	
  "1030 BRANDYWINE ST",
  "214 N 12TH ST",
  "1021 SPRING ST"
)
property1 <- property1 %>%
  mutate(
    central_air = ifelse(location %in% target_locations_N & central_air == "N", "Y", central_air)
  )

# Clean year built field: replace placeholder '1' values and drop invalids
valid_locations <- c(
  "305-09 N 12TH ST",
  "1008-16 WOOD ST",
  "1004-06 WOOD ST",
  "211 N CAMAC ST",
  "231-33 N BROAD ST",
  "225-27 N 12TH ST"
)
property1 <- property1 %>%
  filter(location != "711-39 SPRING GARDEN ST") %>%
  mutate(year_built = as.numeric(year_built)) %>%
  mutate(
    year_built = case_when(
      location == "305-09 N 12TH ST" & year_built < 1750 ~ 1950,
      location == "1008-16 WOOD ST" & year_built < 1750 ~ 1978,
      location == "1004-06 WOOD ST" & year_built < 1750 ~ 1920,
      location == "211 N CAMAC ST" & year_built < 1750 ~ 1900,
      location == "231-33 N BROAD ST" & year_built < 1750 ~ 2020,
      location == "225-27 N 12TH ST" & year_built < 1750 ~ 2024,
      !is.na(year_built) & year_built < 1750 & !(location %in% valid_locations) ~ NA_real_,
      TRUE ~ year_built
    )
  )
```

```{r census data2, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, quiet = TRUE, results='hide',eval=FALSE}
### The method here for pushing data is diffenrent from the one we usually use cause the there is some issues when downloading the geometry data
# census block group
census_api_key("92998588496b9701036218b765c78d2ffb7aedcd", install = TRUE, overwrite = TRUE)
acs_variable_list.2023 <- load_variables(2023, "acs5", cache = TRUE)

local_shapefile <- "Dataset/census/tl_2023_42_bg"
bg_pa <- st_read(local_shapefile, quiet = TRUE)
bg_philly <- bg_pa %>%
  filter(COUNTYFP == "101") %>%
  st_transform(2272) %>%
  select(GEOID, geometry)

block2023_attr <- get_acs(
  geography = "block group",
  variables = c("B19013_001E", "B25058_001E"),
  year = 2023,
  state = 42,
  county = 101,
  geometry = FALSE
)

block2023_attr <- block2023_attr %>%
  select(GEOID, variable, estimate) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = variable, values_from = estimate) %>%
  rename(
    MedHHInc = B19013_001,
    MedRent = B25058_001
  )

block2023 <- left_join(bg_philly, block2023_attr, by = "GEOID")

studyarea_blockgroup_df <- as.data.frame(studyarea_blockgroup) %>% select(-geometry)
block2023_studyarea <- block2023 %>% inner_join(studyarea_blockgroup_df, by = "GEOID")

#census tract
tract_pa <- st_read("Dataset/census/tl_2023_42_tract", quiet = TRUE)

tract_philly <- tract_pa %>%
  filter(COUNTYFP == "101") %>%
  st_transform(2272) %>%
  select(GEOID, geometry)

tract_attr <- get_acs(
  geography = "tract",
  variables = c("B25026_001E", "B15001_050E", "B15001_009E","B06012_002E"),
  year = 2023, state = 42, county = 101, geometry = FALSE
)

tract_attr_wide <- tract_attr %>%
  select(GEOID, variable, estimate) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = variable, values_from = estimate) %>%
  rename(
    TotalPop = B25026_001,
    FemaleBachelors = B15001_050,
    MaleBachelors = B15001_009,
    TotalPoverty = B06012_002
  )

tract2023 <- left_join(tract_philly, tract_attr_wide, by = "GEOID")
studyarea_blockgroup_df <- as.data.frame(studyarea_blockgroup) %>% select(-geometry)

tract2023 <- tract2023 %>%
  mutate(GEOID_trimmed = as.numeric(str_sub(GEOID, 7, 9)))

studyarea_blockgroup_df <- studyarea_blockgroup_df %>%
  mutate(GEOID_trimmed = as.numeric(str_sub(TRACT, 2, 4)))

tract2023_studyarea <- tract2023 %>%
  inner_join(studyarea_blockgroup_df, by = "GEOID_trimmed")
tract_studyarea <- st_intersection(studyarea, tract2023_studyarea)

# property1_property2_census_join
property1 <- property1 %>%
  mutate(census_tract = as.numeric(census_tract))
tract_studyarea_selected <- tract_studyarea %>%
  select(GEOID_trimmed, TotalPoverty, MaleBachelors, FemaleBachelors, TotalPop) %>%
  st_drop_geometry()  

property1_blockgroup <- st_join(property1, block2023_studyarea %>% select(GEOID, MedHHInc, MedRent), 
                            join = st_intersects)

property1_geometry <- st_geometry(property1)

tract_studyarea_selected <- tract_studyarea_selected %>%
  distinct(GEOID_trimmed, .keep_all = TRUE)
property1 <- property1_blockgroup %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>% 
  left_join(tract_studyarea_selected, by = c("census_tract" = "GEOID_trimmed"))

property1 <- property1 %>%
  mutate(objectid = as.character(objectid))

# property2 includes additional spatial indicators for modeling,
# such as distance to nearest park, transit, hospital, and supermarket
property2 <- property2 %>%
  mutate(objectid = as.character(objectid))
#Join other indicators to cleaned property1
property_combined <- property1 %>%
  left_join(property2, by = "objectid") %>%
  rename(sale_price = sale_price.y)%>%
  select(-sale_price.x)
```

```{r POI2, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, quiet=TRUE, results='hide', eval = FALSE}
# POI - restaurant-drink-dessert
api_key <- "AIzaSyCa-yuy1Y3n07URlR2HHg6dp_cIEouv9hs"
keywords <- c("restaurant", "dim sum restaurant", "kitchen", "desert","tea", "bubble tea","matcha", "herbal tea")
place_types <- c("restaurant", "cafe", "bakery")

studyarea_proj <- st_transform(block2023_studyarea, 2272)

grid_pts <- st_make_grid(studyarea_proj, cellsize = 2000, what = "centers")
grid_pts <- st_sf(geometry = grid_pts) %>%
  st_filter(st_buffer(studyarea_proj, 1000)) 

grid_pts_wgs <- st_transform(grid_pts, 4326)
coords <- st_coordinates(grid_pts_wgs)

all_responses <- list()

for (pt_idx in seq_len(nrow(coords))) {
  location <- coords[pt_idx, c(2,1)]  # lat, lng
  cat(" Querying center point", pt_idx, "at", paste(location, collapse = ", "), "\n")
  
  for (ptype in place_types) {
    for (kw in keywords) {
      Sys.sleep(5)  
      cat("🔎", kw, "in", ptype, "\n")

      response <- google_places(
        keyword = kw,
        location = location,
        radius = 2000,  
        place_type = ptype,
        key = api_key
      )

      if (is.null(response[["results"]]) || length(response[["results"]]) == 0) {
        cat("No results for:", kw, "in", ptype, "\n")
        next
      }

      page_token <- response$next_page_token
      results_list <- list(response[["results"]])
      i <- 1

      while (!is.null(page_token)) {
        Sys.sleep(10)
        response_next <- google_places(
          keyword = kw,
          location = location,
          radius = 2000,
          place_type = ptype,
          key = api_key,
          page_token = page_token
        )

        if (is.null(response_next[["results"]]) || length(response_next[["results"]]) == 0) break

        results_list[[i + 1]] <- response_next[["results"]]
        page_token <- response_next$next_page_token
        i <- i + 1
      }

      all_responses[[paste(kw, ptype, pt_idx, sep = "_")]] <- bind_rows(results_list) %>%
        filter(!is.na(place_id)) %>%
        distinct(place_id, .keep_all = TRUE)
    }
  }
}

  mutate(lat = geometry$location$lat, lng = geometry$location$lng) %>%

clean_property_poi_distances <- function(property_sf) {
  property_sf %>%
    mutate(
      nearest_grocery_dist_m = as.numeric(nearest_grocery_dist),
      nearest_restaurant_dist_m = as.numeric(nearest_restaurant_dist)) %>%
    select(
      -nearest_grocery_dist,
      -nearest_restaurant_dist
    )
}
```

```{r,eval=FALSE}
### Part of Visualizations on Story map

S0_S1_density <- ggplot() +
  
  # Scenario 0: true adjusted sale price
  geom_density(data = property_S1_perc_change %>% filter(adj_sale_price > 100),
               aes(x = adj_sale_price),
               fill = "#eb5600", alpha = 0.6, color = "transparent") +
  
  # Scenario 1: predicted price
  geom_density(data = property_S1_perc_change,
               aes(x = predicted_price),
               fill = "#1a9988", alpha = 0.6, color = "transparent") +

  # median lines
  geom_vline(data = property_S1_perc_change %>% filter(adj_sale_price > 100),
             aes(xintercept = median(adj_sale_price, na.rm = TRUE)),
             linetype = "dashed", color = "#eb5600") +
  
  geom_vline(data = property_S1_perc_change,
             aes(xintercept = median(predicted_price, na.rm = TRUE)),
             linetype = "dashed", color = "#1a9988") +

  # log-scale x-axis
  scale_x_log10(labels = dollar) +
  
  # title with markdown color
  labs(
    x = "Price",
    y = "Density",
    title = glue::glue("<span style='color:#eb5600;'>Scenario 0</span> vs. <span style='color:#1a9988;'>Scenario 1</span>")
  ) +
  
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_markdown(size = 16, face = "bold"),
    legend.position = "none"
  )
ggsave(
  filename = "~/Documents/Upenn/Practicum/2025/Chinatown-Practicum-my/finalresults/S0_S1_median_density.png",
  plot = S0_S1_density,
  height = 5,
  width = 8.5,
  units = "in",
  dpi = 300
)
```

```{r,eval=FALSE}
  rename(predicted_price = adj_sale_price)

property_S0_js <- property_S1_4326 %>%
  select(-predicted_price) %>%
  rename(predicted_price = adj_sale_price) %>%
  mutate(price_group = cut(predicted_price,
    breaks = c(122885, 362767, 458337, 543662, 851036, 1150392, Inf),
    labels = c("Very Low (<363K)",
               "Low (363K–458K)",
               "Lower-Mid (458K–544K)",
               "Upper-Mid (544K–851K)",
               "High (851K–1.15M)",
               "Luxury (≥1.15M)"),
    include.lowest = TRUE,
    right = FALSE
  ))

property_S0_js <- property_S0_js %>%
  mutate(size_scaled = scales::rescale(predicted_price, to = c(3, 15))) 

mapview(property_S0_js)
```
